disclaimer: Causes are ordered from most likely and cheapest to try. Change one thing at a time. Temperatures here are the same starting points as the Fix page, not universal settings.

defects.title: Stringing
defects.symptom: Fine hairs or threads between separate parts of the print.

causes.cause: Wet filament, especially PETG, TPU, or nylon
causes.fix: Dry the spool, then print again before you change retraction.

causes.cause: Nozzle too hot
causes.fix: Drop 5–10 °C, or run a temperature tower.

causes.cause: Retraction too short or too slow
causes.fix: Run a retraction test. Direct drive is often around 0.4–1.5 mm.

causes.cause: Long travels across open air
causes.fix: Turn on avoid-crossing-walls or combing, and place parts closer together.

causes.cause: Pressure advance off
causes.fix: Calibrate pressure advance or flow dynamics.

defects.title: Warping
defects.symptom: Corners lift, or the base curls up off the plate.

causes.cause: The part cools much faster than the air around it (ABS, ASA, PC, nylon)
causes.fix: Close the enclosure, preheat the chamber, and keep drafts and air conditioning off the printer.

causes.cause: Too much part cooling
causes.fix: Turn the fan down or off for ABS, ASA, and PC. Use a little fan only on overhangs.

causes.cause: Weak first-layer grip
causes.fix: Wash the plate, use glue if the material needs it, and check first-layer squish.

causes.cause: Sharp corners on a large footprint
causes.fix: Add a brim or mouse ears. Round the corners in the model if you can.

causes.cause: Printing too fast
causes.fix: Slow the first layers and the outer walls.

defects.title: Layer shift
defects.symptom: Layers step sideways, like a staircase, partway up the print.

causes.cause: The nozzle hit a curled corner or a blob
causes.fix: Fix the warp or the curl. Turn on Z-hop. Cool overhangs more on PLA and PETG.

causes.cause: Loose belt or a pulley grub screw
causes.fix: Set belt tension the way the maker describes. Tighten the grub screw onto the flat of the shaft.

causes.cause: Something blocked the axis
causes.fix: Check cables, filament scraps, and a spool that cannot unwind.

causes.cause: Acceleration too high for this machine
causes.fix: Lower speed and acceleration. Re-run input shaping if the printer has it.

causes.cause: A motor or driver overheating
causes.fix: Make sure the electronics have airflow.

defects.title: Elephant's foot
defects.symptom: The first layers bulge wider than the rest of the part.

causes.cause: Nozzle too close on the first layer
causes.fix: Raise Z-offset a little, or run bed leveling again.

causes.cause: Bed hot enough that the bottom stays soft
causes.fix: Lower the bed 5–10 °C after the first layer.

causes.cause: A heavy part sitting on soft bottom layers
causes.fix: Use elephant's-foot compensation around 0.1–0.2 mm, or chamfer the bottom edge in CAD.

defects.title: Under-extrusion
defects.symptom: Gaps, thin walls, or missing lines. The part looks starved of plastic.

causes.cause: Printing faster than the hotend can melt
causes.fix: Slow down, or set a max volumetric speed from a calibration print.

causes.cause: Partial clog or a worn nozzle
causes.fix: Cold pull, or replace the nozzle. Fiber-filled filament wears brass quickly.

causes.cause: Nozzle too close on the first layer
causes.fix: Re-level and adjust Z-offset.

causes.cause: Dirty extruder gears or wrong idler tension
causes.fix: Clean the gears and check tension.

causes.cause: Heat creep, especially PLA in a closed hot box
causes.fix: Open the lid or door for PLA and check the hotend fan.

causes.cause: Wet filament, a tangle, or drag from a filament changer
causes.fix: Dry the spool and check the path from spool to nozzle.

causes.cause: Flow ratio off
causes.fix: Run a flow calibration.

defects.title: Z-banding
defects.symptom: Regular horizontal ridges repeating up the walls.

causes.cause: Lead screw or Z coupler binding, dirty, or misaligned
causes.fix: Clean the screws, check the coupler, and make sure Z moves freely. Lubricate only where the maker says to.

causes.cause: Layer height fighting the Z motor's step size
causes.fix: Try a layer height the community calls a magic number for that lead screw, often a multiple of 0.04 mm on 8 mm-lead machines.

causes.cause: Bed or hotend temperature swinging
causes.fix: Run PID tuning and check that the thermistor is seated.

causes.cause: Uneven filament diameter or a wet spool
causes.fix: Try a known-good spool.

causes.cause: Loose frame or gantry
causes.fix: Check frame screws and the rollers or linear rails.

defects.title: Bed adhesion
defects.symptom: The first layer will not stick, or the part pops off mid-print.

causes.cause: Oil or fingerprints on the plate
causes.fix: Wash PEI with dish soap and hot water. Wipe with isopropyl alcohol between prints.

causes.cause: Z-offset too high
causes.fix: Lower it until the lines are flat and touching, not round or see-through.

causes.cause: Wrong plate or release agent
causes.fix: PETG on smooth PEI wants glue as a release layer. ABS, ASA, PC, and nylon usually want glue for grip.

causes.cause: Bed temperature off
causes.fix: Start from the material table. Too hot can make PLA sag.

causes.cause: Drafts or a cold room
causes.fix: Close the enclosure. Keep fans and air conditioning off the plate.

causes.cause: Very small contact area
causes.fix: Add a brim, or turn the part so more of it touches the plate.

defects.title: Wet filament
defects.symptom: Popping or hissing at the nozzle, a rough or fuzzy surface, or sudden stringing on a profile that used to work.

causes.cause: The spool absorbed water
causes.fix: Dry it at the temperature and time on the material page, then store it sealed with desiccant.

causes.cause: A profile that used to be fine suddenly strings
causes.fix: Dry the spool before you retune retraction.

causes.cause: Weak layers or filament that snaps
causes.fix: Dry it. If it is still brittle, the spool may be too old to save.

causes.cause: Nylon supports that will not come off
causes.fix: Bambu's support note: remove PA supports within about two hours, before the part drinks moisture.

defects.title: Spaghetti
defects.symptom: A loose nest of filament, usually because the part detached or a layer printed in the air.

causes.cause: The part let go of the plate
causes.fix: Stop the print. Fix adhesion: clean plate, Z-offset, brim, and no drafts.

causes.cause: Nobody noticed the first layer fail
causes.fix: Watch the first layer, or turn on the printer's failure detection if it has a camera.

defects.title: Nozzle clog
defects.symptom: The extruder clicks, plastic stops coming out, or the print turns hollow partway up.

causes.cause: Debris or cooked plastic in the nozzle
causes.fix: Heat the nozzle and do a cold pull using your printer's temperatures, or swap the nozzle.

causes.cause: Heat creep on PLA
causes.fix: Open the enclosure and confirm the hotend fan spins.

causes.cause: Nozzle ground into the plate
causes.fix: Raise Z-offset so the first layer is not transparent.

causes.cause: Fiber-filled filament in a brass nozzle
causes.fix: Fit a hardened nozzle.
